fixer.title: launch skill: record Code OSS demo videos and fix Windows cleanup

introducer.title: launch: improve cross-platform setup and cleanup

cases.mechanism: The cleanup owner used a spelling-sensitive argument comparison and could lose the only targeted handle to still-running Electron processes when Windows represented the same temp directory in short versus long form, retaining the process tree and its 1-4 GB working set after the demo session.
cases.symptom: Windows launch sessions could survive cleanup indefinitely, retaining a full Code OSS Electron process tree and gigabytes of memory until manually terminated.
cases.fixedBehavior: Cleanup now compares the canonical long form of the expected run directory and each `--user-data-dir` value, so short and long spellings select the launched Code OSS process and allow it to be terminated before deleting the profile.
cases.evidence: The base cleanup required an ordinal-insensitive exact `--user-data-dir=<path>` string match before every Stop-Process. The launcher derives that argument from `$env:TEMP` and returns `runDir`, while cleanup reparses the supplied runDir with GetFullPath; Windows short (8.3) and long spellings can therefore name the same directory without matching. The changed call at cleanup.ps1:44 delegates to a path-aware matcher that expands both spellings with GetLongPathName. If the old predicate misses, no Code OSS child is stopped; the documented cleanup path then attempts recursive deletion while the Electron instance remains live. Repository guidance identifies each instance as consuming 1-4 GB and explicitly requires cleanup.
